issues.description: Command names are plural while every adjacent command is singular
issues.detail: The codebase uses quickmark_save, quickmark_load, quickmark_add, bookmark_add, bookmark_load (all singular). This patch adds quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload (plural). That's BAD-TASTE: it overwrites the codebase's voice with the author's. Rename to quickmark_reload and bookmark_reload to match the surrounding code. The maintainer six years from now should not have to remember which commands are plural and which aren't.

Both new scenarios are written as bare 'Scenario:' with no description, while every other scenario in urlmarks.feature has a descriptive title (e.g. 'Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)'). Doesn't match the file's voice. Add titles like 'Reloading bookmarks (:bookmark-reload)' and 'Reloading quickmarks (:quickmark-reload)'.

issues.description: Test does not verify the pre-reload state was loaded
issues.detail: test_reload writes one URL, constructs the manager, writes a different URL, calls reload(), and asserts only the post-reload state. It never asserts that the initial example.com mark was actually present before reload(). The test would pass if __init__ silently did nothing. Add an assertion on bm.marks after construction and before the second write to actually exercise the 'reload replaces' behavior.

issues.description: reload() now emits 'changed' during __init__ before save-manager is connected
issues.detail: Previously __init__ parsed inline and did not emit changed; now it calls reload() which emits changed.emit() before _init_savemanager runs. No listeners are connected yet so this is harmless today, but it's a behavior change with no mention in the commit message. State why the refactor is safe, or have reload() take an emit=True flag and skip the emit during construction.

issues.description: GOOD-TASTE: __init__ refactored to call reload() eliminates duplicate parse logic
issues.detail: The change replaces the in-line parse loop in __init__ with a call to the new reload() method, so the load-from-disk path exists once instead of twice. This is the right shape for the patch. Worth keeping; just noting it as the part of the diff that earned the ACCEPT half of the verdict.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The refactor inside UrlMarkManager is good taste — it removes a duplicated parse loop and exposes the load path as reload(), which is the right shape for this feature. The two new commands are also the right size. The patch is refused in its current form for two concrete reasons: the command names are plural (quickmarks_reload, bookmarks_reload) while every adjacent command in the file is singular, and the new Cucumber scenarios have empty titles where every other scenario in the file has a descriptive one. Rename the commands to quickmark_reload / bookmark_reload, give the scenarios titles, and strengthen the unit test to actually assert the pre-reload state before re-asserting post-reload. Do that and this lands.
